text:
mike_sre: SLO alert fired for hosted-infer-gateway in eu-west-1 — p99 5xx jumped to ~4.8% at 10:05 UTC. Seeing a tight window of 503/502s and 'connection reset' patterns. Dashboard: https://redwood.app/d/hosted-infer/eu-west-1-summary

deploybot: deploy completed by leah_prod @ 09:58 UTC -> gateway-service v2.14.2 :construction: (deploy id dd-907)

leah_prod: on it. any customer calls or specific routes?

sam_support: AcmeCorp reported timeouts + 503s starting ~10:03 UTC. They sent a couple of request ids: rq_8c9a1f, rq_8c9a2b. Pasting their note into #support ticket.

mike_sre: quick grep in logs shows repeated proxy error entries and upstream resets. Sample log query I ran: ```service:gateway region:eu-west-1 status:5xx | group_by(upstream_service, status_code) | count() | sort_desc()``` Results: backend-model (pool) responsible for ~62% of 5xx in the spike window.

miguel_obs: traces are sparse — a lot of requests have ingress spans but no downstream model-worker spans (trace gap 10:03:45 - 10:06:20). Also see handshake failures labelled connection_established=false in the proxy metrics.

leah_prod: infra check — any autoscale or node restarts around 10:00?

mike_sre: infra says no autoscale events. Only the deploy at 09:58. But the timing suggests something warmed up then started dropping. Repro attempt from my laptop: ```curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'X-Request-Id: rq_8c9a1f' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'``` — immediate 502 with upstream reset.

sam_support: forwarded repro to AcmeCorp and asked for full request/response pairs — they returned body size ~1.2KB and multiple retries. Marked P1 for customer.

miguel_obs: digging into model-worker logs for node model-worker-3 at 10:02-10:06: found repeated slab/kern messages and abrupt process exits. Snippet: ```[10:03:12] model-worker-3 ERROR kernel_oom: slab_alloc failed, dropping connection; pid=2145 exit=137``` That aligns with connection resets.

leah_prod: if workers are OOMing they could close sockets mid-request — explain missing traces. Good catch. Any memory/GC spikes on the worker?

mike_sre: memory graphs show a sharp increase on model-worker-3 around 09:59 then a drop at 10:03 when process restarts. Rolling OOMs across the pool could explain the ~4.8% p99.

sam_support: customer asked whether this was caused by our deploy. They want ETA to fix.

miguel_obs: theory: new route in v2.14.2 increased batch size or padding for certain prompt shapes, causing occasional OOM on older GPU nodes. Steps to confirm: (1) check model-worker start args for batch/pad overrides, (2) check container OOM logs, (3) correlate request shapes to failing request ids.

mike_sre: immediate mitigation options: (A) route eu-west-1 traffic to eu-west-2 for affected customers (short-term), (B) bump gateway->backend handshake timeout to 10s, (C) temporarily scale up worker pool or drain the suspect node, (D) rollback canary to previous gateway image.

leah_prod: I'll flip the canary off and schedule a targeted rollback if we confirm v2.14.2 changed batch config. Also initiating a drain of model-worker-3.

deploybot: canary flag toggled off by leah_prod at 10:18 UTC (reacts :white_check_mark:)

mike_sre: added a log query to the incident board and pushed a trace sampling tweak to capture full upstream->worker spans for the next hour. Query used for quick correlation: ```logs | where region='eu-west-1' and request_id in (rq_8c9a1f, rq_8c9a2b) | sort by timestamp```

sam_support: letting AcmeCorp know we've identified likely OOMs on a subset of GPU workers, rolling canary off, offering to shift traffic if they want immediate relief. They asked for incident ticket #INC-2026 for audit.

oncallbot: SLO alert resolved at 10:45 UTC (p99 back to 0.9%) — keep monitoring for residual 5xx.

mike_sre: follow-ups: 1) deep dive into v2.14.2 change that touched batching/pad logic, 2) repro locally with high-pad payloads, 3) add OOM alerting per-worker, 4) create temp failover routing for eu-west-1. Created runbook and linked #INC-2026. (reacts :thumbsup:)

leah_prod: assigning postmortem, will include timeline, root cause, and mitigation plan. Will update ticket and ping stakeholders.

sam_support: customer update sent, they appreciate the quick response. Keeping as P1 until we get postmortem.

miguel_obs: I'll attach the relevant worker logs and trace gaps to the incident. Leaving extended sampling on for 2 hours.

mike_sre: thanks everyone — please continue to post any new 5xx request_ids in this thread.
